 Are Katie Boulter's parents still married? What we know about David and Susan Boulter
 Published 19 Oct 2026 at 8:38 AM 
 by  
 Dalphyne Peterz 
 7 min read 
 Katie Boulter's parents, David and Susan (Sue) Boulter, are no longer together — the couple divorced some time before Katie's professional tennis career took off. Katie's mum, who is divorced from her father David, travels widely to support her daughter. Despite the split, both parents shaped one of Britain's finest tennis players. Their daughter recently married Australian tennis star Alex de Minaur, choosing a Leicestershire village — close to where she grew up — as the setting.

 Key takeaways

 Katie was born on 1 August 1996 in Woodhouse Eaves, Leicestershire .
 Sue Boulter was a county-level tennis player who represented Great Britain as a junior, and introduced Katie to the sport at age five.
 Katie's maternal grandfather, Brian Gartshore , is a beloved family figure who regularly attends her matches.
 Katie married Australian tennis star Alex de Minaur in July 2026 in a private ceremony in Leicestershire.

 Are Katie Boulter's parents still together? 
 Katie's mum is divorced from her father David. No public statement from either parent has confirmed when or why the marriage ended. David Boulter has maintained a lower public profile than Katie's mother, with the family generally keeping personal details private.
 Sue Boulter was a competitive county-level tennis player who also represented Great Britain as a junior, and it was Sue who first introduced Katie to the game around the age of five. Since the separation, Sue travels widely to support her daughter on the professional tour, and has remained a constant presence at major tournaments.

 Who is Sue Boulter? 
 Sue is the parent most openly connected to Katie's career. Sue Boulter is a former tennis coach who played at county level and represented Great Britain in junior categories. Her sporting background gave her the technical vocabulary to nurture Katie from the very beginning.
 Katie's maternal grandparents, Brian and Jill Gartshore, also met through tennis. The sport has run through three generations of the family. Katie shared :
 "My grandma was county captain for 20 years and my grandpa played tennis his whole life. That's actually how they met, so I've kind of grown up with tennis and them being a huge part of it." Who is David Boulter? 
 Katie's father David has maintained a lower public profile, with the family generally keeping personal details private. David Boulter is described as a former keen athlete whose encouragement played a role in Katie's early development in the sport. He has not appeared publicly in the same way Sue has throughout Katie's career.

 Katie Boulter's hometown and family roots 
 Katie Boulter of Great Britain poses for a photo with her Grandad and mother following victory against Karolina Pliskova of Czechia. Photo by Nathan Stirk
 Source: Getty Images Katie Charlotte Boulter was born on 1 August 1996 in Woodhouse Eaves, a quiet village in the Charnwood district of Leicestershire. The Boulter family has deep roots in the county, and Katie has spoken warmly about her upbringing there.
 Katie has an older brother, James, and the two were born in Leicestershire, England. James Boulter is currently a venture capitalist and talent agent.
 She began playing tennis at the age of five, and by the time she was eight, she was already representing Great Britain. According to reports, she completed her education at Loughborough College.
 Katie grew up as a supporter of Leicester City Football Club, a loyalty that has stayed with her into adulthood.
 Katie Boulter's grandfather: Brian Gartshore 
 One of the most heartwarming threads of Katie's story is her bond with her maternal grandfather, Brian Gartshore . He attended her matches during Wimbledon 2022 alongside her mum, and Katie's Instagram is full of photos of the two together — at dinner, watching Leicester City, and on country walks.

 Katie has described him as "literally my idol," saying he "put down the airfield lights at Gatwick and Heathrow" and that they "have some great conversations about nothing to do with tennis."
 At the 2022 Wimbledon, two days after the death of her grandmother, Katie returned to the grass — she wasn't going to miss a chance to play at her grandma's favourite tennis tournament. Her grandfather was right there on Centre Court watching every twist and every turn, and ultimately the emotional celebration that came with an upset victory. She said :
 "I was lucky because my grandpa managed to come down from Leicester, and so we could keep him company and keep supporting him at the same time." He was also in attendance at the 2024 Rothesay Open final and was later spotted in a group photograph taken during the victory celebrations in Nottingham.
 Was David Boulter at Katie's wedding? 
 The wedding took place before a small gathering of close family members in July 2026. According to reports, the couple deliberately opted for a low-key, private ceremony attended only by immediate family. No public reporting has specifically confirmed whether David Boulter attended.

 The couple chose to exchange vows close to the place where the bride grew up and where her parents still live, keeping the ceremony small and deeply personal.
 Alex de Minaur had secretly picked the engagement ring alongside Katie's mum, Sue — a detail that underlines just how central Sue remains to Katie's personal life.
 What Katie says about her family 
 Katie has spoken clearly about how much her family means to her, regardless of her parents' marital status.
 "My family are my biggest inspiration in life and in tennis. They have given everything to me throughout their lives." Katie has also reflected on being very close to her grandparents growing up and being lucky to have them around all the time — they would pick her up from tennis, take her to school, and even wave from the corner of the playground at break time. "They were a huge part of my life," she said.

 Source: Getty Images Katie won the WTA 250 title in Ostrava in February 2026, making it her fourth career WTA title. She also embarked on a new coaching partnership at the start of the year, joining forces with coach Michael Joyce following her split from Biljana Veselinovic.

 In July 2026, Boulter and De Minaur secretly tied the knot in a picturesque Leicestershire village on the final day of Wimbledon. After the wedding, Katie confirmed whether she would use Alex de Minaur's surname at tennis tournaments — a question that generated wide interest among fans.
 In 2026, Boulter also secured a notable win over world No. 2 Elena Rybakina at the HSBC Championships, which she described as among the biggest victories of her career.
 Net worth 
 Katie Boulter's net worth is estimated to be around $2 million as of 2024, with her primary income sources being endorsements and prize money from tennis. Her estimated career prize money stands at approximately US$3,763,049 as of 2025.
 Her income streams include:
 Prize money from WTA Tour events
 Endorsement agreements with Wilson and Nike
 Additional sponsorship from Jaguar, Ralph Lauren, Lexus, and Airbnb
 A philanthropic affiliation with Age UK, a charitable organisation dedicated to the well-being of the elderly
 FAQs 
 Are Katie Boulter's parents still married? No. Katie's mum is divorced from her father David. The exact date of their separation has not been made public.
 Where is Katie Boulter's hometown? Woodhouse Eaves, a quiet village in the Charnwood district of Leicestershire.
 Who is Katie Boulter's mother? Sue Boulter is a former tennis coach who played at county level and represented Great Britain in junior categories.
 Who is Katie Boulter's grandfather? Her maternal grandfather is Brian Gartshore, a much-loved family figure. Katie got emotional after seeing her grandfather's pictures from her Rothesay Open title celebration.
 Was Katie Boulter's father at her wedding? The couple opted for a low-key, private ceremony attended only by immediate family. Public reports have not confirmed whether David Boulter was present.
 When did Katie Boulter get married? Boulter and De Minaur secretly tied the knot in a picturesque Leicestershire village on the final day of Wimbledon in July 2026.
 Does Katie Boulter have siblings? Yes. Katie has an older brother, James, and the two were born in Leicestershire, England.
 What is Katie Boulter's net worth? Her net worth is estimated at around $2 million as of 2024.
